content_of_post_to_comment:
Well, 4-digit Duolingo streak. The aim was to learn Spanish at the start but the goalpost shifted eventually. Duolingo works as a switch at the start of my day. This is the first thing that I do and then execute my routine or plan for the day. Rather than being an app to learn Spanish it has become a device that switches on my brain to clear my to-dos and perform my tasks.

I have cleared multiple exams, got multiple certifications, started my Substack, has become a 100x better investor but one thing stayed constant, Duolingo.

But the aim was never achieved, not even decent in Spanish😬 and the reason why I started no more exists.
comment: The funny thing is the Spanish goal almost became secondary, but the habit itself turned into the real asset. A lot of systems we build start as a tool for one outcome and accidentally become the trigger for consistency in everything else. The streak might be less about language learning now and more about proving you can show up every day.
